name: Julian
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Julian, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Julian, CA: Santa on the Town Hall porch, letters to Santa, gingerbread houses, a light parade and A Christmas Carol in the mountains.
lede: Julian does Christmas the small mountain town way: a Country Christmas tree lighting, a homemade light parade down Main Street, and Santa greeting kids on the porch of Town Hall.
celebrates: The Julian Merchants Association and the Julian Chamber of Commerce run Julian's Country Christmas. It opens with a tree lighting day in the town square with music, craft vendor booths and Santa arriving right after the lights come on. Later, volunteers deck out their cars for the Joy in Julian Light Parade, which travels Main Street three times before a Christmas sing-along at Town Hall. Santa greets children on the Town Hall porch, a Letters to Santa desk waits inside, and the community fills the hall with gingerbread houses. The Julian Cider Mill hosts a Living Nativity on its deck, and the East County Performing Arts Association stages A Christmas Carol at the high school.
lastyear: In 2025 Julian's Country Christmas Tree Lighting and Market took place on Saturday, November 29, with craft vendor booths organized by the Julian Chamber of Commerce. Julian Pathways, a local nonprofit, mixed hot cocoa for locals and visitors and later thanked the chamber for putting together a full schedule of performers, telling families who missed it to mark their calendars for the next tree lighting. Visit Julian posted a video of the 2025 lighting by Que Sera Media on its Country Christmas page.
facts: Julian began with gold. Fred Coleman, a former slave, found gold in a creek near present day Julian in January 1869, and the first hard rock claim was filed on February 22, 1870. Because that was George Washington's birthday, it was named the Washington Mine. Drury Bailey named the town after his cousin Mike Julian, said to be the best looking man of the family. James Madison later brought a wagonload of young apple trees up the mountain, the start of Julian's famous apples.
trains: No train climbs to Julian, which sits at about 4,200 feet in the Cuyamaca Mountains, so a train day means a drive down the mountain. The SPRINTER ends at the Escondido Transit Center, and the MTS Trolley reaches El Cajon to the southwest. Old Poway Park runs the Poway-Midland Railroad on weekends, the San Diego Model Railroad Museum fills a hall in Balboa Park with layouts, and the Pacific Southwest Railway Museum in Campo runs its North Pole Limited each December.
train_links: Short heritage train rides around Old Poway Park, the closest train ride to the Julian backcountry.
Huge model railroad layouts of Southern California lines inside Balboa Park.
traditions: The Julian Merchants Association and the chamber light the town tree with live music, craft vendors and Santa arriving after the lights.
Volunteers decorate their cars with lights and drive Main Street three times, then everyone heads to Town Hall for a sing-along.
Santa on the Town Hall porch
Santa meets children with candy canes on the porch of Julian Town Hall, and the visit is free.
A desk inside Town Hall lets kids write to Santa and post the letter in a porch mailbox for the North Pole.
Residents build gingerbread houses and the chamber shows them inside Town Hall.
The Julian Cider Mill presents a Living Nativity on its Main Street deck.
kidfact: Julian was named because one cousin was the most handsome. Drury Bailey picked his cousin Mike Julian's name for the town instead of his own.
faq: Does Julian have a Christmas tree lighting?

Yes. Julian's Country Christmas begins with a tree lighting day organized by the Julian Merchants Association and the Julian Chamber of Commerce. The day includes live music and craft vendor booths, the tree is lit in the evening, and Santa arrives right after the lights come on to meet the kids. Check the Visit Julian events calendar for this year's schedule.
Where can kids see Santa in Julian?

On the porch of Julian Town Hall at 2129 Main Street. The Julian Merchants Association and the chamber list the visits on the Visit Julian events calendar, Santa hands out candy canes, and the visit is free, with donations welcome. Inside the hall there is a desk where children can write a letter to Santa.
What is the Joy in Julian Light Parade?

It is a small town parade of cars, RVs and trailers that volunteers decorate with holiday lights. The parade travels down Main Street three times so every visitor gets a good look, and afterward families can head into Julian Town Hall for a Christmas sing-along. The chamber invites anyone to sign up and decorate a vehicle.
Is there a Christmas play in Julian?

Yes. The East County Performing Arts Association stages A Christmas Carol at the Julian High School Little Theater each December, a yearly tradition since 2022. The version is written by Don Winslow and Scott Kinney, with reserved seats for adults and students and both evening shows and matinees.
Does it snow in Julian at Christmas?

Sometimes. Julian sits at about 4,200 feet in the Cuyamaca Mountains, and Visit Julian says holiday visitors often feel a nip in the air, smell wood fires and may see snow capped mountains around town. Snow is never guaranteed, so dress in layers and check road conditions before driving up.
